items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I had heard about Clifford Brown, had never met him

ctx.x: went down there, and they let Shelly Manne-- Shelly Manne let him sit in, and of course, Shelly was cutting out from the band; there was Shelly, and Oscar Pettiford on bass, and Gene Ammons was there; (unintelligible) -- that was the band that played More Moon, I think it was, one of those Herds. And Ike played there.

And so Shelly said, "I'm leaving and Woody'd really like to hire you." So as I understand it, Ike didn't have a pot -- didn't have a set of drums; which he never did -- somebody was always buying him some. But his lifestyle was such that he couldn't hold on to anything -- a whole lot of us went through that. However, he wanted to know how much he was paying -- and Ike had asked Shelly how much, and he said, "Well, I'm getting $450 a week." And Willie said, "I'll pay you $350" and Ike said, "No, I can't work for…

But there were so many cats like that in the country, or used to be, you might say. Now, it looks like the youngsters, are fortunate enough, their parents prepared them -- they buy them the best instruments and what not.
